# 8. Message Layer: Message Types and Wire Format

O-CPS defines five message classes. All messages share a common header and are encoded with Canonical Protocol Buffers, schema version 3, using the deterministic serialization rules of protobuf-3.21 or later. The use of protobuf is not a commitment to Google’s implementation; any conformant encoder/decoder is acceptable.

The complete schemas appear in Appendix A. This section describes the classes in narrative form and specifies their rate and priority profiles.

## 8.1 Common Header

Every O-CPS message begins with an O-CPS Header:

```protobuf
message OcpsHeader {
  uint32 version          = 1;  // O-CPS schema version; MUST be 2 for this spec
  uint64 timestamp_ms     = 2;  // ms since Unix epoch, UTC
  bytes  cert_id          = 3;  // 8-byte identifier of the signing pseudonym cert
  uint32 msg_class        = 4;  // 0x01=PerceptionSummary, 0x02=Intent,
                                // 0x03=GroupState, 0x04=Attestation,
                                // 0x05=Telemetry
  uint32 seq              = 5;  // monotonically increasing per-sender counter
  uint32 horizon_m        = 6;  // relevance horizon (meters)
  uint32 lifetime_ms      = 7;  // message validity lifetime after timestamp
}
```

## 8.2 Rate and Priority Profile

The following table specifies the per-class rate ceilings, size envelopes, priority assignments, and ASIL allocations. These are normative.

| **Class** | **Rate** | **Size** | **PC5 PPPP** | **ITS-G5 AC** | **ASIL** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PerceptionSummary | 10–20 Hz | 200–500 B | 3 | AC_VO | ASIL B |
| Intent | 2–10 Hz | 60–120 B | 2 | AC_VO | ASIL C |
| GroupState | 1–5 Hz | 120–240 B | 3 | AC_VI | ASIL C |
| Attestation | 0.1–0.5 Hz | 180–320 B | 5 | AC_BE | QM |
| Telemetry | ≤ 0.1 Hz | ≤ 1 KB | 7 | AC_BE | QM |

Notes on the allocation: PerceptionSummary is ASIL B because a corrupted perception message could induce an inappropriate advisory gap target, but the integrator’s ADAS retains ASIL D authority for the actual actuation, which limits upstream allocation. Intent is ASIL C because an Intent message can trigger an actuation-adjacent behavior (a driver-authorized lane change advisory) whose misstatement has higher consequence. GroupState is ASIL C because leader-election faults inside a platoon can induce longitudinal oscillation. Attestation and Telemetry are QM (Quality Management) because their loss degrades trust calibration and diagnostics but does not, in isolation, produce an unsafe actuation.

## 8.3 PerceptionSummary

PerceptionSummary is the workhorse message of O-CPS. Each message conveys the transmitter’s own pose and a list of the objects it currently perceives. Typical transmission rate is 10 Hz in free flow, rising to 20 Hz during maneuvers or in dense traffic, and falling to 2 Hz when stationary in a non-roadway context (e.g., parked).

The message contains:

- The OcpsHeader.
- The transmitter’s own pose (lat, lon, alt, yaw, pitch, roll, speed_mps, longitudinal acceleration).
- The transmitter’s dimensions (length, width, height) in centimeters.
- A list of PerceivedObjects (0–N, N bounded by message-size envelope). Each PerceivedObject contains: class ID, confidence, relative position (range and bearing from transmitter), bounding box (length, width, height), velocity relative to transmitter, and a per-object source sensor mask (bitfield: radar, lidar, camera, ultrasonic, other).
- The ECDSA-P256 signature over the preceding fields.

## 8.4 Intent

Intent is the short-horizon prediction of what the transmitter is about to do. It is used by peers to anticipate maneuvers before they are executed and to coordinate during cooperative behaviors. Transmission is event-driven (on maneuver planning) with a background heartbeat rate of 2 Hz.

The message contains:

- The OcpsHeader.
- An intent code: one of STRAIGHT, LANE_CHANGE_LEFT, LANE_CHANGE_RIGHT, TURN_LEFT, TURN_RIGHT, MERGE, EXIT, STOP, YIELD, PLATOON_FORM, PLATOON_LEAVE.
- A prediction window (ms) over which the intent is valid.
- A confidence score (driver-committed vs. system-predicted).
- An optional GroupState reference (if the intent is group-coupled).
- The signature.

## 8.5 GroupState

GroupState is exchanged among C-ACC Group members to maintain a shared view of membership, ordering, leader identity, and operational mode. Transmission is 1–5 Hz, event-driven on state changes.

The message contains:

- The OcpsHeader.
- A group identifier (128-bit UUID, generated at group formation).
- An ordered list of member pseudonym-cert IDs.
- The leader cert ID.
- The group mode: FORMING, STABLE, HANDOFF, DISSOLVING.
- The active gap target (seconds) and speed setpoint (m/s).
- A monotonic group-epoch counter (incremented on any membership or leadership change).
- The signature.

## 8.6 Attestation

Attestation messages convey a signed claim about the integrity of the transmitter’s O-CPS software stack and its upstream perception pipeline. Transmission is infrequent (0.1–0.5 Hz). The message contains:

- The OcpsHeader.
- A software identifier (vendor OID, stack version, build fingerprint).
- A hash of the currently-loaded O-CPS configuration.
- A boot-time attestation quote from the HSM or TPM (in the format defined by the platform’s attestation service).
- A sensor-stack health summary (count of active sensors by modality, count of degraded sensors).
- The signature.

Receivers use the attestation to apply a trust weight to subsequent PerceptionSummary and Intent messages from the same pseudonym certificate. An attestation older than its lifetime is treated as absent; absence of current attestation is grounds for de-weighting but not for rejection outright, as some conformance classes (notably Class A, §17.1) do not emit attestation.

## 8.7 Telemetry

Telemetry messages are low-rate, non-safety-critical carriers of data useful to operators and road authorities (anonymized road-condition signals, aggregated congestion estimates). They are explicitly subject to the privacy model of §11 and MUST NOT carry any per-trip identifiers.
